transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Nina (Redwood SE), Ryota (Redwood Solutions), Alicia (Skylark HO Search), Ben (Skylark ML Eng), Mark (Skylark CTO), Priya (Skylark Security)

Summary:
Skylark is evaluating options for embeddings + reranking for their product search and QA features. They currently use an internal embedding pipeline and Milvus as the vector store, but they want to reduce latency on rerank, explore hybrid dense+BM25 search, and understand tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (especially around throughput, dimensionality, and VPC/KMS requirements).

Topics:
- Current infra and pain points
- Vector DB integration patterns (Milvus/Pinecone-like)
- Throughput, latency, and batching for 512 vs 1536-dim embeddings
- Hybrid search (BM25 + vector) and reranker placement
- Security/compliance: VPC, KMS, retention, audit logs
- Next steps and benchmarking plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:06] Alicia: hi I'm alicia, head of search at skylark, we run product search and a support QA assistant, we've been iterating on embeddings and rerank for the last year.
[00:12] Ben: ben here, ml eng, I own ingestion, embedding pipeline, and the milvus cluster.
[00:17] Mark: mark, cto, I'll jump in on infra questions.
[00:20] Priya: priya, security, I'll be focusing on VPC/KMS and data residency.
[00:24] Nina: nina from redwood, hi! I work on deployments and perf testing.
[00:27] Samir: cool. quick agenda, high level discovery for embeddings/rerank, then tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated/private, then action items.

[00:40] Samir: can you walk us through current flow? what's the pipeline look like for queries -> rerank?
[00:46] Ben: sure. user query -> we run BM25 over elastic, then we also generate 1536-dim embed for query and do vector search in milvus, top 200 candidates we then rerank with a cross-encoder model that we host on a GPU service.
[01:02] Alicia: that reranker is where we see latency spikes, sometimes 700-900ms p95 when load is up, and costs are creeping.
[01:09] Nina: got it. and you're doing hybrid by unioning BM25 + vect, correct?
[01:14] Ben: yeah it's union plus score fusion, then rerank. We've tried sparse + dense rerank variants.

[01:25] Ryota: what's your current qps for search endpoints?
[01:28] Alicia: avg 25 qps, peak 120 qps during promos. Reranker load is bursty.
[01:36] Samir: do you batch for the reranker?
[01:38] Ben: minimal batching now, we prioritized latency, but we lose cost efficiency.

[01:45] Nina: ok, that's a common pattern. Redwood can offer continuous batching + KV cache to keep p95 down while saving token cost, and for rerankers we surface batching policies you can tune. With Dedicated you can get predictable throughput for the reranker and the embedding generation.

[02:05] Priya: security question up front - any hosted option will need enclave for embeddings? we need KMS integration and audit logs, and our legal group requires SOC2 plus a few data retention rules.
[02:17] Samir: yes. we have Hosted with encrypted at rest and TLS in transit, KMS integrations for customer key support on Dedicated and Private, and audit logs in Redwood Console. For Private we can do customer-managed KMS and VPC with private control plane.
[02:33] Priya: ok, we'll send the SOC2 scope but want to know which path gives us the least friction - hosted might be quick but Private is preferable if there are residency/KMS constraints.

[02:45] Ben: on vector store integration - right now we push vectors to Milvus. how do you usually integrate with customer vector DBs? do you recommend switching to Redwood-hosted vector store?
[02:56] Nina: two common patterns: 1) Redwood does embeddings and returns vectors; you push to existing vector DB and we call out to it for nearest neighbor. 2) Redwood Hosted + Redwood Vector Store (we support persistent stores) where we handle storage and retrieval with optimized sharding. If you need to keep Milvus for legacy reasons, we integrate via the vector API and can support hybrid architecture.
[03:17] Ben: interesting. latency difference?
[03:19] Ryota: depends on deployment and network topology. Dedicated co-located with your Milvus or using Redwood Vector Store in same region can lower NN lookup time. We usually see 10-40ms differences in NN lookup depending on indexing and dimensionality.

[03:36] Alicia: dimensionality question - we're on 1536 dims for now, thinking about switching to 768 to reduce cost. how does dim change affect quality vs perf?
[03:46] Nina: lower dims reduce storage and NN latency; recall might drop depending on model. We often recommend evaluating a smaller dimensional model pairwise on your devset; Redwood Optimize can run an automated sweep to report expected recall vs latency. For reranking cost, the cross-encoder dominating cost, but embedding size affects vector search time and memory footprint.

[04:10] Ben: what's your recommended quantization? we tried int8 and saw quality slippage.
[04:14] Ryota: quantization for embeddings often is safe to 8-bit for certain models; for cross-encoders you should be careful. Redwood's runtime has quantization-friendly execution paths and we can show quality regression tests.

[04:30] Samir: you mentioned reranker placement - do you run the reranker in the same infra as nearest-neighbor?
[04:34] Ben: currently reranker is separate GPU service; that's where most latency and cost are.
[04:38] Nina: options: run reranker as a Dedicated pool reserved for you (predictable SLOs), or run on Redwood Hosted with autoscale and fallback to cheaper models. For tight p95 we advise colocating reranker close to NN to reduce RTTs.

[04:56] Mark: for Dedicated, what's typical sizing for 120 qps peak?
[05:00] Ryota: depends on reranker batchability; with batching and a 1536 input, an 8x batch on A100 equiv gives roughly 200-300 synchronous rerank/s for a medium cross-encoder. For strict tail latency, you might need multiple GPUs to handle bursty spikes. We can propose a sizing doc.

[05:22] Alicia: how about hybrid search - do you recommend retrieving 200 candidates or 100?
[05:27] Nina: we usually start with 200 and experiment. 200 gives better recall for aggressive BM25 failures, but increases reranker load. Redwood Optimize can run evals across candidate sizes to find knee in quality vs cost.

[05:40] Ben: what about vector index types - HNSW vs IVF? we use HNSW in milvus and it's memory heavy.
[05:48] Ryota: HNSW is great for recall and p95 latency, but needs RAM; IVF + PQ is more space efficient but sometimes higher latency for recall-critical queries. For production at scale we often suggest HNSW for low-latency retrieval unless memory is a blocker.

[06:05] Priya: on compliance, what does Private buy us vs Dedicated? specifically for KMS and audit log retention.
[06:11] Samir: Private gives you private control plane and on-prem option; you manage networking and keys. Dedicated offers customer KMS integration and stronger isolation but control plane is still with Redwood. For strict residency and air-gap, Private on-prem is the route.

[06:28] Alicia: any gotchas integrating Redwood outputs with an existing Milvus?
[06:31] Nina: two things - vector layout/normalization and dimensionality must match; if you change model embeddings (e.g., 1536->768) you need to reindex. Also watch for float vs quantized storage compatibility. We can share a short guide for Milvus integration and a migration checklist.

[06:55] Ben: benchmark question - can you run a throughput test where we push our sample 50k vectors and run 100 concurrent queries to simulate our peak?
[07:02] Nina: yes. we can run a small benchmark on Hosted or Dedicated. we can run on a Dedicated trial cluster or on Redwood-hosted staging; we'll need your sample dataset and typical query distribution.

[07:18] Samir: we'll capture that as an action item - Ben to share sample dataset and query patterns.

[07:25] Priya: another note - we need to know data retention options for embeddings, do you allow TTLs or custom retention policies per project?
[07:33] Samir: yes, Redwood Console supports retention policies and we can configure per-account TTLs; for Private you can do custom retention controlled by you.

[07:42] Ben: question on costs - how do you break out pricing for embeddings vs reranker?
[07:46] Samir: hosted is per-embedding unit + per-token/rerank call. Dedicated is reserved GPU + lower per-token costs; we'll send a pricing sheet comparing the three (hosted, dedicated, private) with example run-rate numbers based on your qps and candidate sizes.

[08:05] Mark: any limits on dimensions or vector types? we sometimes use float16 vectors.
[08:10] Ryota: Redwood supports common vector sizes up to several thousand dims and float16/float32; storage and index type selection matter. We recommend sticking to standard float32 unless you have a specific reason.

[08:25] Alicia: curious about caching, you mentioned KV cache earlier - can that help our reranker latency?
[08:30] Nina: KV cache is mostly for autoregressive generation; for rerankers you can use result caching for common queries and prefix caching for repeated sessions. Also embedding cache can avoid recomputing for identical queries. That helps reduce cost and tail latency.

[08:49] Ben: any prebuilt connectors to Milvus? would prefer not to build glue ourselves.
[08:53] Nina: we have integrations and example connectors for Milvus, Pinecone, and Weaviate - sample code in our docs and repo. We'll share links.

[09:05] Samir: ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.

[09:08] Samir: items: 1) Samir to send pricing + Dedicated sizing 2) Nina to run throughput benchmark with 50k sample when Ben sends dataset 3) Priya to send SOC2/compliance questions 4) schedule a technical deep dive on hybrid search and index tuning week of 3/16.

[09:27] Alicia: that sounds good. any final questions?
[09:30] Mark: none here. thanks.

[09:33] Ben: i'll share the sample set by monday.

[09:36] Priya: i'll consolidate compliance questions and ping you.

[09:40] Samir: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and put the deep dive on the calendar.

End of transcript.
